---- MODULE W4Od2m3p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Capacity, MaxTerm

VARIABLES leader, term, docked, crashed, pending

vars == <<leader, term, docked, crashed, pending>>

\* A dock master (leader) is elected among non-crashed robots and alone may
\* grant bay slots. Robots can crash silently, so a separate Failover step
\* notices a crashed dock master before a fresh election can run.
\* BayWithinCapacity is the safety property: occupancy of the shared bay must
\* never exceed the fixed slot Capacity, regardless of crashes or failover.

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Robots \cup {"None"}
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ docked \subseteq Robots
  /\ crashed \subseteq Robots
  /\ pending \subseteq Robots

Init ==
  /\ leader = "None"
  /\ term = 0
  /\ docked = {}
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ pending = {}

ElectLeader ==
  /\ leader = "None"
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ \E r \in Robots \ crashed :
       /\ leader' = r
       /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<docked, crashed, pending>>

CrashSilently ==
  /\ Cardinality(crashed) < Cardinality(Robots) - 1
  /\ \E r \in Robots \ crashed :
       crashed' = crashed \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, docked, pending>>

Failover ==
  /\ leader # "None"
  /\ leader \in crashed
  /\ leader' = "None"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, docked, crashed, pending>>

RequestDock ==
  /\ \E r \in (Robots \ crashed) \ (docked \cup pending) :
       pending' = pending \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, docked, crashed>>

GrantDock ==
  /\ leader # "None"
  /\ leader \notin crashed
  /\ Cardinality(docked) < Capacity
  /\ \E r \in pending :
       /\ docked' = docked \cup {r}
       /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashed>>

Undock ==
  /\ \E r \in docked :
       docked' = docked \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashed, pending>>

Next ==
  \/ ElectLeader
  \/ CrashSilently
  \/ Failover
  \/ RequestDock
  \/ GrantDock
  \/ Undock

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BayWithinCapacity == Cardinality(docked) <= Capacity

====

CONSTANTS
  Robots = {r1, r2, r3}
  Capacity = 2
  MaxTerm = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BayWithinCapacity
nl:
A fleet of warehouse robots shares a single staging bay with a fixed number of
docking slots. One robot at a time acts as the fleet's dock master: it is chosen
by a leader election among the robots that are not known to be crashed, and it
is the only robot allowed to grant a robot access to a docking slot. Robots that
want to charge or load cargo first join a request queue. The dock master, while
it is alive, pulls robots from the queue and admits them to the bay only if the
bay has not reached its slot capacity; robots later finish and undock, freeing a
slot. The twist is that any robot -- including the currently recognized dock
master -- can crash silently: it simply stops taking any further action, with no
message telling the rest of the fleet. Because the crash is silent, the fleet
does not immediately know the dock master is gone; a separate failover step is
needed to notice that the recognized dock master is among the crashed robots and
clear the role so a new election can pick a replacement. Granting a slot always
requires the dock master identity to point at a robot that has not (yet, as far
as the fleet's bookkeeping is concerned) been marked crashed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of robots simultaneously occupying the shared
docking bay never exceeds the bay's fixed slot capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od12m8p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Requesters, TotalUnits

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, queue, available, reserved, issued

vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, queue, available, reserved, issued>>

\* Hierarchical locking: a technician must hold the coarse fridge-wide lock
\* before it can take the finer bin-level lock and move a unit into
\* "reserved". Conservation is the invariant: available+reserved+issued is
\* fixed. ReleaseLocks is unconditional once the coarse lock is held, which is
\* what lets a slow-but-never-failing technician always finish eventually.

Init ==
  /\ coarseLock = "None"
  /\ fineLock = "None"
  /\ queue = {}
  /\ available = TotalUnits
  /\ reserved = 0
  /\ issued = 0

RequestAccess(r) ==
  /\ r \notin queue
  /\ coarseLock # r
  /\ fineLock # r
  /\ queue' = queue \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, available, reserved, issued>>

AcquireCoarse(r) ==
  /\ r \in queue
  /\ coarseLock = "None"
  /\ coarseLock' = r
  /\ queue' = queue \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, available, reserved, issued>>

AcquireFineAndTransfer(r) ==
  /\ coarseLock = r
  /\ fineLock = "None"
  /\ available > 0
  /\ fineLock' = r
  /\ available' = available - 1
  /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, queue, issued>>

ReleaseLocks(r) ==
  /\ coarseLock = r
  /\ coarseLock' = "None"
  /\ fineLock' = "None"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, available, reserved, issued>>

IssueUnit ==
  /\ reserved > 0
  /\ issued' = issued + 1
  /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, queue, available>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Requesters : RequestAccess(r)
  \/ \E r \in Requesters : AcquireCoarse(r)
  \/ \E r \in Requesters : AcquireFineAndTransfer(r)
  \/ \E r \in Requesters : ReleaseLocks(r)
  \/ IssueUnit

Fairness == \A r \in Requesters : WF_vars(ReleaseLocks(r))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

Conservation == available + reserved + issued = TotalUnits

CoarseLockEventuallyReleased == []<>(coarseLock = "None")

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Requesters = {t1, t2}
  TotalUnits = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT Conservation
PROPERTY CoarseLockEventuallyReleased
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker manages a fixed pool of blood units stored in a
shared fridge. Every unit is always accounted for in exactly one of three
buckets: sitting available in the fridge, reserved for a specific patient, or
already issued out to a ward. Access to the fridge is protected by a two-level
hierarchical lock: a technician must first acquire the coarse, fridge-wide lock
before they are allowed to acquire the finer bin-level lock that lets them
actually move a unit from "available" to "reserved" for the patient they are
serving. Technicians who want fridge access first join a wait queue, then take
the coarse lock once it is free, then take the fine lock to perform the
transfer. Ward staff separately issue previously reserved units to patients,
moving units from "reserved" to "issued". The twist is that a technician
holding the locks can be slow -- paperwork, a busy ward, interruptions -- but
is never assumed to fail or disappear: every technician who takes the coarse
lock is always eventually going to release both the coarse and fine lock, it
just may take a while.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state the number of units available, plus
the number reserved, plus the number issued, equals the fixed total pool size
-- no unit is ever created or destroyed by requesting, locking, transferring,
or issuing.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: once a technician acquires the coarse fridge-wide lock, that
lock is always eventually released, so the fridge never stays permanently
inaccessible to the rest of the queue.

---- MODULE W4Od5m5p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Capacity, Quorum

VARIABLES lobby, pending, votesFor, banned

vars == <<lobby, pending, votesFor, banned>>

\* Quorum voting: a pending player is normally seated only once enough seated
\* players vote yes for them. The admin override bypasses the vote and, if
\* the lobby is full, bumps someone out (into a short ban) to make room; that
\* override is what guarantees every pending request is eventually resolved.
\* SeatsWithinCapacity is the safety property: the lobby never overfills.

Init ==
  /\ lobby = {}
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ votesFor = [p \in Players |-> {}]
  /\ banned = {}

RequestJoin(p) ==
  /\ p \notin lobby
  /\ p \notin pending
  /\ p \notin banned
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {p}
  /\ votesFor' = [votesFor EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, banned>>

CastVote(voter, p) ==
  /\ voter \in lobby
  /\ p \in pending
  /\ voter \notin votesFor[p]
  /\ votesFor' = [votesFor EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {voter}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, pending, banned>>

AdmitByQuorum(p) ==
  /\ p \in pending
  /\ Cardinality(votesFor[p]) >= Quorum
  /\ Cardinality(lobby) < Capacity
  /\ lobby' = lobby \cup {p}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votesFor, banned>>

AdminOverrideAdmit(p) ==
  /\ p \in pending
  /\ IF Cardinality(lobby) < Capacity
     THEN /\ lobby' = lobby \cup {p}
          /\ banned' = banned
     ELSE \E victim \in lobby :
            /\ lobby' = (lobby \ {victim}) \cup {p}
            /\ banned' = banned \cup {victim}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED votesFor

Leave(p) ==
  /\ p \in lobby
  /\ lobby' = lobby \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, votesFor, banned>>

Unban(p) ==
  /\ p \in banned
  /\ banned' = banned \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, pending, votesFor>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Players : RequestJoin(p)
  \/ \E voter \in Players, p \in Players : CastVote(voter, p)
  \/ \E p \in Players : AdmitByQuorum(p)
  \/ \E p \in Players : AdminOverrideAdmit(p)
  \/ \E p \in Players : Leave(p)
  \/ \E p \in Players : Unban(p)

Fairness == \A p \in Players : WF_vars(AdminOverrideAdmit(p))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

SeatsWithinCapacity == Cardinality(lobby) <= Capacity

PendingAlwaysResolved == \A p \in Players : (p \in pending) ~> (p \notin pending)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Players = {p1, p2, p3}
  Capacity = 2
  Quorum = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SeatsWithinCapacity
PROPERTY PendingAlwaysResolved
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker fills a lobby that has a fixed maximum
number of seats. Any player may ask to join, which puts them in a pending
queue. Admitting a pending player normally requires a quorum vote: enough of
the players already seated in the lobby must cast a yes vote for that
candidate before the matchmaker is allowed to seat them, and seating only
happens if the lobby still has a free seat. Seated players may leave whenever
they like, freeing their seat. The twist is that the matchmaker also exposes a
privileged admin override: an admin can seat a pending player immediately,
skipping the quorum vote entirely, and if the lobby is already full the
override is strong enough to bump one existing seated player out (placing them
in a short-lived ban list) to make room for the incoming player. A banned
player cannot re-request a seat until the ban is lifted.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of players simultaneously seated in the lobby never
exceeds the lobby's fixed seat capacity, whether players are seated through
quorum voting or through the admin override.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every player who is placed in the pending queue is
eventually resolved out of the queue -- either seated by quorum vote or seated
by the admin override -- and never left waiting forever.

---- MODULE W4Od8m1p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS N, Seats

Nodes == 0..(N-1)
NextInRing(n) == (n + 1) % N

VARIABLES token, crashed, available, enrolled, lastHolder

vars == <<token, crashed, available, enrolled, lastHolder>>

\* Token ring: only the current token holder may touch the enrollment ledger.
\* Nodes are numbered 0..N-1 and NextInRing fixes the cyclic hand-off order.
\* A server can crash silently and is simply marked crashed; the token still
\* keeps circulating (PassToken while alive, DetectAndSkip past a crashed
\* holder). Conservation is the invariant: available+enrolled is fixed --
\* no seat is ever created or destroyed.

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Nodes
  /\ crashed \subseteq Nodes
  /\ available \in 0..Seats
  /\ enrolled \in 0..Seats
  /\ lastHolder \in Nodes \cup {N}

Init ==
  /\ token \in Nodes
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ available = Seats
  /\ enrolled = 0
  /\ lastHolder = N

PassToken ==
  /\ token \notin crashed
  /\ lastHolder' = token
  /\ token' = NextInRing(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, available, enrolled>>

DetectAndSkip ==
  /\ token \in crashed
  /\ lastHolder' = token
  /\ token' = NextInRing(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, available, enrolled>>

CrashSilently ==
  /\ \E n \in Nodes \ crashed :
       crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, available, enrolled, lastHolder>>

EnrollStudent ==
  /\ token \notin crashed
  /\ available > 0
  /\ available' = available - 1
  /\ enrolled' = enrolled + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, crashed, lastHolder>>

DropStudent ==
  /\ token \notin crashed
  /\ enrolled > 0
  /\ enrolled' = enrolled - 1
  /\ available' = available + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, crashed, lastHolder>>

Next ==
  \/ PassToken
  \/ DetectAndSkip
  \/ CrashSilently
  \/ EnrollStudent
  \/ DropStudent

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Conservation == available + enrolled = Seats

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  N = 3
  Seats = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A university course-registration system protects the enrollment ledger for one
course with a fixed number of seats. A single access token circulates around a
fixed ring of registrar servers, and only the server currently holding the
token is allowed to move a seat between the "available" bucket and the
"enrolled" bucket -- one enrollment or one drop at a time. The token holder
passes the token on to the next server in ring order when it is done, and a
watchdog can also nudge the token past a server that turns out to be dead. The
twist is that any registrar server, including the one currently holding the
token, can crash silently: it just stops acting, with no announcement to the
rest of the ring. A crashed server is simply marked crashed in the fleet's
bookkeeping; it never enrolls or drops a seat while marked that way, and the
token is free to keep moving around the ring regardless of which servers have
crashed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, the number of available seats plus
the number of enrolled seats equals the course's fixed seat total -- no seat
is ever created or destroyed by enrolling, dropping, passing the token, or a
server crashing.

---- MODULE W4Od12m2p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Slots, Hospitals, Participants

\* Two-phase commit over refrigerated slots: a round moves free -> pending ->
\* committed -> free. Commit only fires once every live participant has voted
\* yes; Abort fires once a crashed participant makes full agreement impossible.
VARIABLES slotOwner, roundHospital, roundStatus, votes, crashed

vars == <<slotOwner, roundHospital, roundStatus, votes, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ slotOwner \in [Slots -> Hospitals \cup {"NONE"}]
    /\ roundHospital \in [Slots -> Hospitals \cup {"NONE"}]
    /\ roundStatus \in [Slots -> {"free", "pending", "committed"}]
    /\ votes \in [Slots -> SUBSET Participants]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Participants

Init ==
    /\ slotOwner = [s \in Slots |-> "NONE"]
    /\ roundHospital = [s \in Slots |-> "NONE"]
    /\ roundStatus = [s \in Slots |-> "free"]
    /\ votes = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
    /\ crashed = {}

StartRoundAction(s, h) ==
    /\ roundStatus[s] = "free"
    /\ roundHospital' = [roundHospital EXCEPT ![s] = h]
    /\ roundStatus' = [roundStatus EXCEPT ![s] = "pending"]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, crashed>>

VoteAction(s, p) ==
    /\ roundStatus[s] = "pending"
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ p \notin votes[s]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {p}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, roundHospital, roundStatus, crashed>>

CommitAction(s) ==
    /\ roundStatus[s] = "pending"
    /\ votes[s] = Participants
    /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = roundHospital[s]]
    /\ roundStatus' = [roundStatus EXCEPT ![s] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roundHospital, votes, crashed>>

AbortAction(s) ==
    /\ roundStatus[s] = "pending"
    /\ \E p \in Participants : p \in crashed /\ p \notin votes[s]
    /\ roundStatus' = [roundStatus EXCEPT ![s] = "free"]
    /\ roundHospital' = [roundHospital EXCEPT ![s] = "NONE"]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, crashed>>

CrashAction(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ \E s \in Slots : roundStatus[s] = "pending" /\ p \notin votes[s]
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, roundHospital, roundStatus, votes>>

ReleaseAction(s) ==
    /\ roundStatus[s] = "committed"
    /\ roundStatus' = [roundStatus EXCEPT ![s] = "free"]
    /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = "NONE"]
    /\ roundHospital' = [roundHospital EXCEPT ![s] = "NONE"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots, h \in Hospitals : StartRoundAction(s, h)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, p \in Participants : VoteAction(s, p)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : CommitAction(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AbortAction(s)
    \/ \E p \in Participants : CrashAction(p)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : ReleaseAction(s)

Fairness ==
    /\ \A s \in Slots, p \in Participants : WF_vars(VoteAction(s, p))
    /\ \A s \in Slots : WF_vars(CommitAction(s))
    /\ \A s \in Slots : WF_vars(AbortAction(s))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

SafeAllocation ==
    \A s \in Slots :
        /\ (roundStatus[s] = "committed" => slotOwner[s] = roundHospital[s])
        /\ (slotOwner[s] # "NONE" => roundStatus[s] = "committed")

EventuallyResolved ==
    \A s \in Slots : (roundStatus[s] = "pending") ~> (roundStatus[s] # "pending")

====
nl:
A regional blood-bank network keeps a small pool of refrigerated storage slots
that hold reserved units of blood. Hospitals request a slot be reserved for a
scheduled transfusion. Each reservation runs through a two-phase-commit
protocol: a coordinator asks every participant bank to "prepare" a candidate
slot, waits for all live participants to vote, and only then "commits" the
allocation, writing exactly one hospital ID into the slot record. If any
participant votes no, or the coordinator times out waiting on a participant,
the coordinator aborts the round and the slot returns to the free pool so a
later round can retry it. One participant bank can crash silently at any time
after voting "yes" and before the coordinator's decision reaches it: it simply
stops responding, and the coordinator must still reach a decision (using the
votes it already collected) rather than block forever. The tracker's actions
are: a coordinator starting a prepare round on a free slot, a participant
casting a prepare vote, the coordinator committing the round once all
participants have voted yes, the coordinator aborting the round (on a no vote
or on detecting the silent crash) and freeing the slot, and the silent crash
of a participant during a pending round.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two committed rounds ever hold the same slot allocated to two different hospitals at once, and a slot's allocated hospital is always one that actually reserved it through a committed round.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every prepare round that is started is eventually resolved -- it is either committed or aborted, it never stays pending forever, even when a participant crashes silently.

---- MODULE W4Od8m1p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Advisors, MaxGen

N == Cardinality(Advisors)
RingNext(a) == IF a = N THEN 1 ELSE a + 1

NextAlive(a, crashedSet) ==
    LET c == RingNext(a)
    IN  IF c \notin crashedSet THEN c ELSE RingNext(c)

VARIABLES tokenHolder, editingAdvisor, crashed, tokenGen, editGen

vars == <<tokenHolder, editingAdvisor, crashed, tokenGen, editGen>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ tokenHolder \in Advisors
    /\ editingAdvisor \in Advisors \cup {0}
    /\ crashed \subseteq Advisors
    /\ tokenGen \in 0..MaxGen
    /\ editGen \in 0..MaxGen

Init ==
    /\ tokenHolder \in Advisors
    /\ editingAdvisor = 0
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ tokenGen = 0
    /\ editGen = 0

OpenAction(a) ==
    /\ tokenHolder = a
    /\ a \notin crashed
    /\ editingAdvisor = 0
    /\ editingAdvisor' = a
    /\ editGen' = tokenGen
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, crashed, tokenGen>>

CloseAndPassAction(a) ==
    /\ tokenHolder = a
    /\ a \notin crashed
    /\ editingAdvisor = a
    /\ editingAdvisor' = 0
    /\ tokenHolder' = NextAlive(a, crashed)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, tokenGen, editGen>>

CrashAction(a) ==
    /\ tokenHolder = a
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, editingAdvisor, tokenGen, editGen>>

RegenerateAction ==
    /\ tokenHolder \in crashed
    /\ tokenGen < MaxGen
    /\ tokenHolder' = NextAlive(tokenHolder, crashed)
    /\ tokenGen' = tokenGen + 1
    /\ editingAdvisor' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, editGen>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Advisors : OpenAction(a)
    \/ \E a \in Advisors : CloseAndPassAction(a)
    \/ \E a \in Advisors : CrashAction(a)
    \/ RegenerateAction

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LiveTokenCoherence ==
    editingAdvisor # 0 => (editingAdvisor = tokenHolder /\ editGen = tokenGen)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Advisors = {1, 2, 3}
    MaxGen = 3
INVARIANT LiveTokenCoherence
nl:
A university's course-registration system lets department advisors edit the
single shared seat-count ledger for a popular capped course. To prevent two
advisors from writing conflicting seat counts at once, the advisors are
arranged in a logical ring and pass a single edit token around it: only the
advisor currently holding the token may open the ledger for editing, and it
must release the token (passing it to the next advisor in ring order) before
anyone else may open the ledger again. One advisor's workstation can crash
silently while holding the token -- it simply stops responding and never
passes the token onward -- so the system also lets a monitor process notice a
stalled holder and regenerate the token at the next advisor in the ring,
retiring the old one, so registration edits are not permanently locked out by
a single crashed workstation. The system's actions are: an advisor acquiring
the token to open the ledger for editing, that advisor closing the ledger and
passing the token to the next advisor in ring order, an advisor's workstation
crashing silently while it holds the token, and the monitor regenerating a
fresh token at the next advisor after a crashed holder is detected.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one advisor has the ledger open for editing at any time, and only the advisor who currently holds a live (non-retired) token may have it open.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Blocks, Controllers, Values, AdminBudget

VARIABLES record, version, requestBlock, requestVal, requestBase, adminBudget

vars == <<record, version, requestBlock, requestVal, requestBase, adminBudget>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \in [Blocks -> Values]
    /\ version \in [Blocks -> Nat]
    /\ requestBlock \in [Controllers -> Blocks \cup {"NONE", "DONE"}]
    /\ requestVal \in [Controllers -> Values]
    /\ requestBase \in [Controllers -> Nat]
    /\ adminBudget \in 0..AdminBudget

Init ==
    /\ record \in [Blocks -> Values]
    /\ version = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ requestBlock = [c \in Controllers |-> "NONE"]
    /\ requestVal = [c \in Controllers |-> CHOOSE v \in Values : TRUE]
    /\ requestBase = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ adminBudget = AdminBudget

SubmitAction(c, b, val) ==
    /\ requestBlock[c] = "NONE"
    /\ requestBlock' = [requestBlock EXCEPT ![c] = b]
    /\ requestVal' = [requestVal EXCEPT ![c] = val]
    /\ requestBase' = [requestBase EXCEPT ![c] = version[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, adminBudget>>

ApplySuccessAction(c) ==
    /\ requestBlock[c] \in Blocks
    /\ requestBase[c] = version[requestBlock[c]]
    /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![requestBlock[c]] = requestVal[c]]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![requestBlock[c]] = @ + 1]
    /\ requestBlock' = [requestBlock EXCEPT ![c] = "DONE"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requestVal, requestBase, adminBudget>>

RetryAction(c) ==
    /\ requestBlock[c] \in Blocks
    /\ requestBase[c] # version[requestBlock[c]]
    /\ requestBase' = [requestBase EXCEPT ![c] = version[requestBlock[c]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, requestBlock, requestVal, adminBudget>>

AdminOverrideAction(b, val) ==
    /\ adminBudget > 0
    /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![b] = val]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ adminBudget' = adminBudget - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requestBlock, requestVal, requestBase>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Blocks, val \in Values : SubmitAction(c, b, val)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : ApplySuccessAction(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : RetryAction(c)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks, val \in Values : AdminOverrideAction(b, val)

Fairness ==
    /\ \A c \in Controllers : WF_vars(ApplySuccessAction(c))
    /\ \A c \in Controllers : WF_vars(RetryAction(c))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

NoLostUpdates ==
    \A c \in Controllers : requestBlock[c] \in Blocks => requestBase[c] <= version[requestBlock[c]]

EventuallyApplied ==
    \A c \in Controllers : (requestBlock[c] \in Blocks) ~> (requestBlock[c] = "DONE")

====
nl:
A subway line's signalling block keeps one shared occupancy/speed-restriction
record. Traffic controllers update it through a compare-and-swap register:
a controller first reads the record's current version tag, then submits a
write carrying that tag as its expected version; the write only lands if the
tag still matches the block's live version, otherwise the controller must
re-read the live version and resubmit rather than blindly clobbering
whatever change happened in between. A privileged operations-center admin
can also force-write the record directly, bypassing the compare-and-swap
check entirely -- but every admin write still bumps the block's version tag,
so any controller whose expected tag is now stale is forced to re-read and
retry instead of silently losing the admin's change (or having the admin's
change silently lost). The admin's override budget for a given run is
limited, modelling that overrides are for genuine emergencies rather than a
routine substitute for the compare-and-swap path. The system's actions are:
a controller submitting a write request against the record's current
version, the controller's write landing once its expected version matches
the live one, the controller re-reading the live version and refreshing its
expected tag after a mismatch, and the admin force-writing the record and
bumping its version.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A controller's expected version tag is never ahead of the block's true live version -- no controller can regard its own record view as more current than reality, so no write can silently clobber a change it never saw.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every write a controller submits is eventually applied to the record, even if the admin's overrides force it to re-read and resubmit first.

credits: the total number of credits in the swarm never changes, only how

needing the leader's involvement at all -- for example to hand a patrol
directly to a better-positioned drone -- but even this override only moves
an existing credit, it never manufactures a new one or drops one on the
floor. The swarm's actions are: the leader checking a credit out of the pool
to a drone, the leader checking a credit back into the pool from a drone,
the current leader failing over to a newly elected drone for the next term,
and the admin directly transferring a checked-out credit from one drone to
another.

Bump(v) == IF v = VMod - 1 THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

VARIABLES capacity, pool, engaged, version, myVersion

vars == <<capacity, pool, engaged, version, myVersion>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCapacity
    /\ pool \in 0..MaxCapacity
    /\ engaged \in [Locks -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ version \in 0..(VMod - 1)
    /\ myVersion \in [Locks -> 0..(VMod - 1)]

Init ==
    /\ capacity = InitialCapacity
    /\ pool = InitialCapacity
    /\ engaged = [l \in Locks |-> FALSE]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ myVersion = [l \in Locks |-> 0]

SyncAction(l) ==
    /\ ~engaged[l]
    /\ myVersion[l] # version
    /\ myVersion' = [myVersion EXCEPT ![l] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, pool, engaged, version>>

AcquireAction(l) ==
    /\ ~engaged[l]
    /\ myVersion[l] = version
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ engaged' = [engaged EXCEPT ![l] = TRUE]
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ version' = Bump(version)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, myVersion>>

ReleaseAction(l) ==
    /\ engaged[l]
    /\ engaged' = [engaged EXCEPT ![l] = FALSE]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ version' = Bump(version)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, myVersion>>

AddHubAction ==
    /\ capacity < MaxCapacity
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ version' = Bump(version)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<engaged, myVersion>>

RetireHubAction ==
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ version' = Bump(version)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<engaged, myVersion>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Locks : SyncAction(l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : AcquireAction(l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : ReleaseAction(l)
    \/ AddHubAction
    \/ RetireHubAction

Fairness == \A l \in Locks : WF_vars(SyncAction(l))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

Conservation ==
    pool + Cardinality({l \in Locks : engaged[l]}) = capacity

EventuallySynced ==
    \A l \in Locks : (~engaged[l] /\ myVersion[l] # version) ~> (engaged[l] \/ myVersion[l] = version)

    Locks = {l1, l2}

    InitialCapacity = 1

PROPERTY EventuallySynced
nl:
A smart-home's door-lock network shares a pool of simultaneous unlock
grants: at any moment the number of grants sitting free in the central pool
plus the number currently held by engaged locks must equal the network's
current capacity. A lock that wants to hold a grant keeps a locally cached
copy of the pool's ledger version; it may only take a free grant when its
cached version still matches the ledger's true version (a compare-and-swap
check), and if the ledger has moved on since it last looked, the lock must
re-read the ledger version before it can try again -- this stops two locks
from racing onto the same grant and stops a lock from acting on a
picture of the pool that's already out of date. The network's capacity is
not fixed: the homeowner can add a battery hub, which mints one more grant
directly into the pool, or retire one, which removes one currently-free
grant from the pool, and either change bumps the ledger version so every
idle lock's cached view is immediately known to be stale. A lock also
releases its held grant back to the pool whenever its door re-locks. The
network's actions are: an idle lock re-reading the ledger's true version
after finding its cached copy stale, an idle lock taking a free grant from
the pool because its cached version matches the ledger, an engaged lock
releasing its held grant back to the pool, the homeowner adding a battery
hub to mint one grant into capacity, and the homeowner retiring a hub to
remove one free grant from capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The free grants in the pool plus the grants held by engaged locks always equal the network's current capacity, exactly -- no grant is ever minted, retired, or lost except through an explicit capacity change.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every idle lock whose cached ledger view has gone stale -- whether from another lock's activity or from a capacity change -- eventually either re-syncs to the true version or becomes engaged.

---- MODULE W4Od18m7p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Doors, Clients, MaxVer

NoDoor == "none"
NoneWriter == "none"
AdminWriter == "admin"

VARIABLES ver, locked, holder, writeBasis, cachedVer, pending

\* ver/locked/holder form the shared per-door record; writeBasis records the
\* version each door's last successful writer (client CAS or admin) acted on.
\* cachedVer/pending model a client's read-then-swap sequence for CAS.
\* MaxVer bounds the version counter purely to keep the model finite.

TypeOK ==
  /\ ver \in [Doors -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ locked \in [Doors -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ holder \in [Doors -> Clients \cup {AdminWriter, NoneWriter}]
  /\ writeBasis \in [Doors -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ cachedVer \in [Clients -> 0..MaxVer]
  /\ pending \in [Clients -> Doors \cup {NoDoor}]

Init ==
  /\ ver = [d \in Doors |-> 0]
  /\ locked = [d \in Doors |-> FALSE]
  /\ holder = [d \in Doors |-> NoneWriter]
  /\ writeBasis = [d \in Doors |-> 0]
  /\ cachedVer = [c \in Clients |-> 0]
  /\ pending = [c \in Clients |-> NoDoor]

\* A client begins a lock/unlock attempt by reading a door's current version.
StartRequest(c, d) ==
  /\ pending[c] = NoDoor
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = d]
  /\ cachedVer' = [cachedVer EXCEPT ![c] = ver[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, locked, holder, writeBasis>>

\* A client's compare-and-swap succeeds only if its cached version still
\* matches the door's true stored version at the moment of the write.
CasSucceed(c) ==
  /\ pending[c] # NoDoor
  /\ LET d == pending[c] IN
       /\ cachedVer[c] = ver[d]
       /\ ver[d] < MaxVer
       /\ locked' = [locked EXCEPT ![d] = ~locked[d]]
       /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![d] = ver[d] + 1]
       /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![d] = c]
       /\ writeBasis' = [writeBasis EXCEPT ![d] = ver[d]]
       /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = NoDoor]
  /\ UNCHANGED cachedVer

\* A stale cached version means the swap is rejected; the client abandons
\* the attempt instead of clobbering whoever wrote the door in the meantime.
CasFail(c) ==
  /\ pending[c] # NoDoor
  /\ LET d == pending[c] IN
       /\ cachedVer[c] # ver[d]
       /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = NoDoor]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, locked, holder, writeBasis, cachedVer>>

\* The administrator's emergency override bypasses the client CAS protocol
\* entirely but still writes against the door's true current version.
AdminOverride(d) ==
  /\ ver[d] < MaxVer
  /\ locked' = [locked EXCEPT ![d] = ~locked[d]]
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![d] = ver[d] + 1]
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![d] = AdminWriter]
  /\ writeBasis' = [writeBasis EXCEPT ![d] = ver[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cachedVer, pending>>

\* A client's app can also time out or cancel a pending attempt without
\* completing it, e.g. the user closed the app before the swap resolved.
CancelRequest(c) ==
  /\ pending[c] # NoDoor
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![c] = NoDoor]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, locked, holder, writeBasis, cachedVer>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Clients, d \in Doors : StartRequest(c, d)
  \/ \E c \in Clients : CasSucceed(c)
  \/ \E c \in Clients : CasFail(c)
  \/ \E d \in Doors : AdminOverride(d)
  \/ \E c \in Clients : CancelRequest(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<ver, locked, holder, writeBasis, cachedVer, pending>>

\* No lost updates: every door's most recent successful write was based on
\* the version immediately preceding the door's current version, so no
\* completed write ever silently skipped or clobbered a prior update.
NoLostUpdates == \A d \in Doors : ver[d] > 0 => writeBasis[d] = ver[d] - 1

====
nl:
A smart-home platform manages a small network of connected door locks. Each door's status is a shared record (lock state, version counter, and last writer) that mobile-app clients update using compare-and-swap (CAS). Before changing a lock, a client's app must first read the door's current version number into a local cache, then submit a swap request tagged with that cached version; the smart-home hub only accepts the swap if the cached version still matches the door's stored version at the moment the request lands, otherwise the swap is rejected and the app must re-read and retry later. This CAS discipline is what keeps two family members' phones from clobbering each other's toggle of the same lock.

The system also has a privileged home-administrator role (e.g. a property manager or emergency responder) who can force a lock's state to flip immediately without going through the read-then-swap dance. This bypass exists for emergencies, but it must still stamp the record with a fresh version and identify itself as the writer, so that any client's later CAS attempt against the version it read before the override is correctly rejected rather than silently overwriting the administrator's action.

Actions: (1) a client begins a lock/unlock attempt by reading the target door's current version into its local cache; (2) a client whose cached version still matches the door's stored version successfully performs the compare-and-swap, flipping the lock state and bumping the version, and records the version it swapped against as the write's basis; (3) a client whose cached version has gone stale (no longer matches) has its swap rejected and simply abandons the attempt, making no change to the door record; (4) the administrator can override any door's state at any time, always writing against the door's true current version and likewise recording that version as the write's basis; (5) a client's app can also cancel or time out a pending attempt without completing it (e.g. the user closed the app before the swap resolved), simply abandoning the request.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a door's lock record shows a nonzero version number, the version basis recorded for that door's most recent successful write (whether performed by a client's CAS or by the administrator's override) is exactly one less than the door's current version -- meaning no completed write for any door was ever based on a stale or skipped version, so no update to the shared lock record is ever silently lost.

---- MODULE W4Od3m4p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Participants, Cap

\* queue is the bounded backlog (backpressure via the Cap guard on Submit).
\* active is the set of banks currently holding the shared settlement
\* engine; the mutual-exclusion invariant asserts it never holds two.
\* crashed/done track a bank's terminal outcome; the watchdog action
\* reclaims the engine from a crashed holder so progress cannot stall.
VARIABLES queue, active, crashed, done

QueueSet == {queue[i] : i \in 1..Len(queue)}

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(Participants)
  /\ active \subseteq Participants
  /\ crashed \subseteq Participants
  /\ done \subseteq Participants

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ active = {}
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ done = {}

\* Backpressure: a bank may submit only while the backlog is below Cap and
\* it has no request already pending or in progress.
Submit(p) ==
  /\ p \notin QueueSet
  /\ p \notin active
  /\ Len(queue) < Cap
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, p)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<active, crashed, done>>

\* The engine, if idle, pulls the head of the backlog into exclusive use.
AcquireResource ==
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ active = {}
  /\ active' = active \cup {Head(queue)}
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, done>>

\* A healthy holder finishes and releases the engine.
ReleaseResource(p) ==
  /\ p \in active
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ active' = active \ {p}
  /\ done' = done \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed>>

\* A bank can silently crash whether waiting or currently holding the engine.
CrashSilently(p) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, active, done>>

\* The watchdog detects a crashed holder and forcibly frees the engine.
ReclaimCrashedHolder ==
  /\ \E p \in active : p \in crashed
  /\ LET p == CHOOSE q \in active : q \in crashed IN
       active' = active \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed, done>>

ReleaseAction == \E p \in Participants : ReleaseResource(p)
CrashAction == \E p \in Participants : CrashSilently(p)

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Submit(p)
  \/ AcquireResource
  \/ ReleaseAction
  \/ CrashAction
  \/ ReclaimCrashedHolder

vars == <<queue, active, crashed, done>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
          /\ WF_vars(AcquireResource)
          /\ WF_vars(ReleaseAction)
          /\ WF_vars(ReclaimCrashedHolder)

\* Mutual exclusion: no two distinct banks ever hold the engine together.
MutualExclusion == \A p, q \in active : p = q

\* A bank in the backlog or holding the engine.
InSystem(p) == p \in QueueSet \/ p \in active

\* Liveness: every bank that enters the system eventually settles or is
\* discovered crashed -- it never stays stuck in limbo forever.
Progress == \A p \in Participants : InSystem(p) ~> (p \in done \/ p \in crashed)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Participants = {p1, p2, p3}
  Cap = 2
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY Progress
nl:
A group of banks settle interbank transfers through a shared nightly settlement batch. Each bank submits its settlement request into a bounded backlog queue maintained by the clearing house; the backlog has a fixed capacity, and once it is full the clearing house exercises backpressure -- it simply refuses new submissions until a slot frees up. The clearing house's settlement engine itself is a single critical resource: it can only work on one bank's batch at a time, pulling the next request from the front of the backlog once it is free.

The twist is that a participant bank can crash silently at any point -- whether while its request is still sitting in the backlog or, worse, right after it has been granted exclusive access to the settlement engine. A crash while holding the engine would jam clearing for every other bank forever unless the clearing house's watchdog notices the silent failure and forcibly reclaims the engine so the queue can keep moving.

Actions: (1) a bank submits a settlement request, which is appended to the backlog only if the backlog is below capacity (backpressure blocks submission otherwise); (2) the settlement engine, when idle, acquires exclusive access by pulling the request at the front of the backlog; (3) the bank currently holding the engine finishes normally, releasing the engine and recording its settlement as complete; (4) a bank can crash silently at any time, whether queued or holding the engine; (5) if the bank currently holding the engine has crashed, the watchdog reclaims the engine (freeing it without crediting a completion) so that other banks' requests can still be processed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: at no point do two distinct banks simultaneously hold exclusive access to the shared settlement engine.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bank whose request is in the backlog or currently being processed is eventually either recorded as having completed settlement or discovered to have crashed -- the shared engine, combined with the watchdog's crash reclamation, never leaves a bank's request stuck in limbo forever.

---- MODULE W4Od18m8p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Zones, Controllers

\* Each zone has one fine-grained door beneath it; hierarchical acquisition
\* means a door lock may only be granted to a controller that currently
\* holds the coarse zone lock covering that door. Requests travel through
\* the two inbox sets below; because a set has no order, the hub may see
\* requests in an order different from when controllers sent them, modeling
\* network reordering. The invariant checks that reordering never lets two
\* controllers hold the same door lock at once.
Doors == Zones \X {1}
ZoneOf(d) == d[1]

VARIABLES zoneLock, doorLock, zoneReqInbox, doorReqInbox

TypeOK ==
  /\ zoneLock \in [Zones -> SUBSET Controllers]
  /\ doorLock \in [Doors -> SUBSET Controllers]
  /\ zoneReqInbox \subseteq (Controllers \X Zones)
  /\ doorReqInbox \subseteq (Controllers \X Doors)

Init ==
  /\ zoneLock = [z \in Zones |-> {}]
  /\ doorLock = [d \in Doors |-> {}]
  /\ zoneReqInbox = {}
  /\ doorReqInbox = {}

\* A controller asks for the coarse lock on a zone.
SendZoneRequest(c, z) ==
  /\ zoneReqInbox' = zoneReqInbox \cup {<<c, z>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, doorLock, doorReqInbox>>

\* The hub grants any pending, still-valid zone request; the request it
\* picks need not be the oldest one, modeling reordering.
HubGrantZone ==
  /\ \E cz \in zoneReqInbox : zoneLock[cz[2]] = {}
  /\ LET cz == CHOOSE p \in zoneReqInbox : zoneLock[p[2]] = {} IN
       /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![cz[2]] = zoneLock[cz[2]] \cup {cz[1]}]
       /\ zoneReqInbox' = zoneReqInbox \ {cz}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<doorLock, doorReqInbox>>

\* A controller may only ask for a door's fine lock while it holds the
\* zone lock covering that door.
SendDoorRequest(c, d) ==
  /\ c \in zoneLock[ZoneOf(d)]
  /\ doorReqInbox' = doorReqInbox \cup {<<c, d>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, doorLock, zoneReqInbox>>

\* The hub re-checks zone ownership at grant time, since a door request
\* accepted earlier may have gone stale due to reordering/delay.
HubGrantDoor ==
  /\ \E cd \in doorReqInbox : doorLock[cd[2]] = {} /\ cd[1] \in zoneLock[ZoneOf(cd[2])]
  /\ LET cd == CHOOSE p \in doorReqInbox :
                 doorLock[p[2]] = {} /\ p[1] \in zoneLock[ZoneOf(p[2])] IN
       /\ doorLock' = [doorLock EXCEPT ![cd[2]] = doorLock[cd[2]] \cup {cd[1]}]
       /\ doorReqInbox' = doorReqInbox \ {cd}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, zoneReqInbox>>

\* A door holder releases its fine lock.
ReleaseDoor(c, d) ==
  /\ c \in doorLock[d]
  /\ doorLock' = [doorLock EXCEPT ![d] = doorLock[d] \ {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneLock, zoneReqInbox, doorReqInbox>>

\* A zone holder releases its coarse lock, but only after giving up every
\* door lock it holds beneath that zone.
ReleaseZone(c, z) ==
  /\ c \in zoneLock[z]
  /\ \A d \in Doors : ZoneOf(d) = z => c \notin doorLock[d]
  /\ zoneLock' = [zoneLock EXCEPT ![z] = zoneLock[z] \ {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<doorLock, zoneReqInbox, doorReqInbox>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, z \in Zones : SendZoneRequest(c, z)
  \/ HubGrantZone
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, d \in Doors : SendDoorRequest(c, d)
  \/ HubGrantDoor
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, d \in Doors : ReleaseDoor(c, d)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, z \in Zones : ReleaseZone(c, z)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<zoneLock, doorLock, zoneReqInbox, doorReqInbox>>

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: a door's fine-grained lock
\* is never held by two distinct controllers at once, even though request
\* messages may be reordered on their way to the hub.
DoorMutex == \A d \in Doors : \A c1, c2 \in doorLock[d] : c1 = c2

====
nl:
A smart-home vendor organizes a house's door locks into zones (e.g. "front entrance", "garage") and enforces a hierarchical locking discipline: a controller app must first acquire the coarse-grained zone lock before it is allowed to request the fine-grained lock on an individual door actuator inside that zone. Both lock levels are requested by sending a message to the smart-home hub -- a zone-lock request or a door-lock request -- and the hub grants the request once it observes the message and the resource is free.

The twist is that these request messages travel over an unreliable local network and can be reordered or delayed arbitrarily; the hub does not see messages in the order the controllers sent them. This means a door-lock request that was valid when sent (because the controller held the zone lock at that moment) might not reach the hub until well after the controller released the zone lock, or after a different controller took it. To stay safe, the hub must re-check that the requesting controller still holds the zone lock at the moment it actually grants the door lock, not merely trust that the request was valid when it was sent.

Actions: (1) a controller sends a zone-lock request for a zone; (2) the hub grants a pending zone-lock request to its controller if that zone is currently free; (3) a controller that currently holds a zone's lock sends a door-lock request for a door inside that zone; (4) the hub grants a pending door-lock request only if the target door is free AND the requesting controller still holds that door's zone lock at the moment of granting (protecting against a stale, reordered request); (5) a controller holding a door lock releases it; (6) a controller holding a zone lock releases it, but only once it holds no door locks left inside that zone (fine locks must be released before the coarse lock, preserving the hierarchy).

SAFETY PROPERTY: for every individual door, at most one controller ever holds that door's fine-grained lock at the same time -- reordered network messages never let two controllers simultaneously actuate the same door.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m2p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Participants

\* holder is the (at most singleton) set of stations currently allowed to
\* actuate the shared dispensing cabinet; txn/votes model an in-progress
\* two-phase-commit round granting that access; crashed models the twist
\* that a controller node can silently stop responding to votes. The
\* Commit action treats a crashed voter as automatically satisfied so a
\* round is never blocked forever by an unresponsive node.
VARIABLES holder, txn, votes, crashed

TypeOK ==
  /\ holder \subseteq Participants
  /\ txn \in Participants \cup {"none"}
  /\ votes \in [Participants -> {"unasked", "yes"}]
  /\ crashed \subseteq Participants

Init ==
  /\ holder = {}
  /\ txn = "none"
  /\ votes = [p \in Participants |-> "unasked"]
  /\ crashed = {}

\* A free station begins a 2PC round to request exclusive cabinet access.
StartTxn(p) ==
  /\ txn = "none"
  /\ holder = {}
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ txn' = p
  /\ votes' = [q \in Participants |-> "unasked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

\* A live, not-yet-voted station confirms it isn't using the cabinet.
CastVote(q) ==
  /\ txn # "none"
  /\ votes[q] = "unasked"
  /\ q \notin crashed
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![q] = "yes"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, txn, crashed>>

\* Commit once every live station has voted yes; crashed stations count as
\* satisfied automatically so the round is never stuck on a dead node.
Commit ==
  /\ txn # "none"
  /\ txn \notin crashed
  /\ \A q \in Participants : q \in crashed \/ votes[q] = "yes"
  /\ holder' = holder \cup {txn}
  /\ txn' = "none"
  /\ votes' = [q \in Participants |-> "unasked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* If the requester itself crashed before committing, abandon the round.
AbortTxn ==
  /\ txn # "none"
  /\ txn \in crashed
  /\ txn' = "none"
  /\ votes' = [q \in Participants |-> "unasked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

\* At most one controller node ever crashes silently in this model.
CrashSilently(q) ==
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ crashed' = {q}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, txn, votes>>

\* The station holding the cabinet finishes and releases it.
Release(p) ==
  /\ p \in holder
  /\ holder' = holder \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<txn, votes, crashed>>

CastVoteAction == \E q \in Participants : CastVote(q)

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Participants : StartTxn(p)
  \/ CastVoteAction
  \/ Commit
  \/ AbortTxn
  \/ \E q \in Participants : CrashSilently(q)
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Release(p)

vars == <<holder, txn, votes, crashed>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
          /\ WF_vars(CastVoteAction)
          /\ WF_vars(Commit)
          /\ WF_vars(AbortTxn)

\* Mutual exclusion: no two distinct stations ever hold cabinet access
\* at the same time.
CabinetMutex == \A p, q \in holder : p = q

\* Liveness: a round that starts for a requester is always eventually
\* resolved, one way or the other -- it never hangs forever.
Progress == \A p \in Participants : (txn = p) ~> (txn = "none")

CONSTANTS
  Participants = {p1, p2, p3}
INVARIANT CabinetMutex
PROPERTY Progress
nl:
A hospital pharmacy has one automated dispensing cabinet (the critical resource) shared by several dispensing stations, each running its own local controller node. Because the cabinet's drawer mechanism can physically serve only one station's dispense operation at a time, the stations use a two-phase-commit protocol to hand out exclusive access safely: a station that wants to dispense starts a round by asking every other station's controller node to confirm it isn't about to use the cabinet itself; once every live node has voted yes, the round commits and the requesting station is granted exclusive access. When it finishes, it releases the cabinet so the next round can start.

The twist is that a controller node can crash silently at any moment, including in the middle of a voting round, and it will never send a vote. If the coordinator simply waited forever for that node's vote, the cabinet would freeze up and nobody could dispense again. Instead, the protocol recognizes a crashed node as effectively voting "not in the way" for the purposes of committing, so a round can still be committed once every still-live node has voted yes. If the crash happens to strike the requesting station itself before its own round commits, the round is abandoned instead of granting a phantom station exclusive access.

Actions: (1) a station with the cabinet currently free starts a two-phase-commit round to request exclusive access; (2) any other live station that has not yet voted in the current round casts a "yes" vote confirming it isn't using the cabinet; (3) once every live station has voted yes (crashed stations are treated as satisfying the vote), the round commits and the requesting station is granted exclusive access to the cabinet; (4) if the requesting station itself has crashed before its round committed, the round is abandoned and the protocol returns to idle; (5) a single controller node can crash silently at any time (at most one node ever crashes in this model); (6) the station holding the cabinet finishes and releases it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: at no point do two distinct stations simultaneously hold exclusive access to the dispensing cabinet.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every two-phase-commit round that starts for a requesting station is eventually resolved -- it either commits, granting that station the cabinet, or is abandoned because the requester crashed -- so a silently crashed voter can never leave a round stuck forever.

---- MODULE W4Od4m2p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Lanes, MaxSlots

\* Slots 1..capacity are the conveyor's currently active positions; capacity
\* can rise or fall at runtime. occupancy records which lane's car sits in
\* which slot as a set of pairs, so the invariant can genuinely check that
\* no slot appears twice with different lanes, rather than relying on a
\* function's shape to rule that out by construction. txn/acked model a
\* two-phase-commit round allocating one proposed slot at a time.
Slots == 1..MaxSlots

VARIABLES capacity, occupancy, txn, acked

TypeOK ==
  /\ capacity \in 0..MaxSlots
  /\ occupancy \subseteq (Lanes \X Slots)
  /\ txn \in (Slots \X Lanes) \cup {"none"}
  /\ acked \subseteq Lanes

SlotFree(s) == \A p \in occupancy : p[2] # s

Init ==
  /\ capacity = MaxSlots
  /\ occupancy = {}
  /\ txn = "none"
  /\ acked = {}

\* The operator resizes the active conveyor, even mid-round.
ChangeCapacity(newCap) ==
  /\ newCap \in 0..MaxSlots
  /\ newCap # capacity
  /\ capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, txn, acked>>

\* A lane proposes to allocate a currently active, apparently free slot.
ProposeAllocate(l, s) ==
  /\ txn = "none"
  /\ s <= capacity
  /\ SlotFree(s)
  /\ txn' = <<s, l>>
  /\ acked' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, occupancy>>

\* Another lane re-checks its own replica before acknowledging.
Ack(l2) ==
  /\ txn # "none"
  /\ l2 \notin acked
  /\ SlotFree(txn[1])
  /\ acked' = acked \cup {l2}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, occupancy, txn>>

\* Commit only if the targeted slot is still active and free at this
\* moment; a mutated/omitted recheck here is exactly what could let two
\* lanes end up occupying the same slot.
Commit ==
  /\ txn # "none"
  /\ acked = Lanes
  /\ txn[1] <= capacity
  /\ SlotFree(txn[1])
  /\ occupancy' = occupancy \cup {<<txn[2], txn[1]>>}
  /\ txn' = "none"
  /\ acked' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED capacity

\* If the targeted slot went out of service or was filled meanwhile,
\* abandon the round instead of committing a stale allocation.
AbortStale ==
  /\ txn # "none"
  /\ (txn[1] > capacity \/ ~SlotFree(txn[1]))
  /\ txn' = "none"
  /\ acked' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, occupancy>>

\* A finished car vacates its slot.
Vacate(l, s) ==
  /\ <<l, s>> \in occupancy
  /\ occupancy' = occupancy \ {<<l, s>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, txn, acked>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in 0..MaxSlots : ChangeCapacity(n)
  \/ \E l \in Lanes, s \in Slots : ProposeAllocate(l, s)
  \/ \E l2 \in Lanes : Ack(l2)
  \/ Commit
  \/ AbortStale
  \/ \E l \in Lanes, s \in Slots : Vacate(l, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<capacity, occupancy, txn, acked>>

\* No double allocation: no two distinct lanes ever occupy the same slot.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A p1, p2 \in occupancy : p1[2] = p2[2] => p1[1] = p2[1]

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Lanes = {l1, l2}
  MaxSlots = 2
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A car wash runs a single conveyor line with a fixed set of physical slots where cars sit while being washed. Multiple entry lanes feed cars onto the conveyor, and each lane runs its own controller with a locally replicated view of which slots are occupied. To allocate an incoming car to a slot safely across these replicated controllers, the lane that wants a slot runs a two-phase-commit round: it proposes a specific free, currently active slot, every other lane's controller re-checks its own replica and acknowledges that the slot still looks free, and only once every lane has acknowledged does the proposing lane commit the allocation.

The twist is that the conveyor's active capacity changes at runtime -- the operator can take a slot out of service (for a jam or maintenance) or bring a new one online while a two-phase-commit round is already under way. If a slot that was targeted by an in-flight proposal gets taken out of service before the round commits, the round must be abandoned rather than committed, since committing would place a car on a slot the conveyor no longer considers active. A slot that is already occupied by a car keeps that car until the car is done, regardless of any capacity change.

Actions: (1) the operator changes the number of active slots at runtime, which can happen at any time, including while a round is in progress; (2) a lane with no round currently in progress proposes to allocate a currently active slot that appears free in its own replica; (3) another lane acknowledges the proposal after re-checking that the slot still appears free in its own replica; (4) once every lane has acknowledged, and the targeted slot is still active and free, the round commits and the slot becomes occupied by the proposing lane's car; (5) if the targeted slot has since gone out of service or become occupied, the round is instead abandoned without allocating anything; (6) the car occupying a slot finishes washing and vacates it, freeing the slot for a future round.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no two distinct lanes are ever recorded as occupying the same conveyor slot at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od15m4p0t1 ----
\* Opening-auction order gateway: a bounded work queue with backpressure feeds
\* a single matching engine (the critical resource). Orders carry no intrinsic
\* arrival order, so admission into the queue may happen in any relative order,
\* modeling in-flight message reordering. EngineMutex guards the critical
\* resource; EventualMatch is the progress guarantee the queue+engine owe
\* every admitted order.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Orders, Cap

VARIABLES queue, inEngine, matched, rejected

vars == <<queue, inEngine, matched, rejected>>

Range(s) == {s[i] : i \in 1..Len(s)}

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(Orders)
  /\ inEngine \subseteq Orders
  /\ matched \subseteq Orders
  /\ rejected \subseteq Orders

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ inEngine = {}
  /\ matched = {}
  /\ rejected = {}

\* Backpressure: an order enters the bounded queue only while there is room.
\* Because Orders has no built-in arrival order, any not-yet-seen order may be
\* admitted next, which is how in-flight message reordering is represented.
Submit ==
  \E o \in Orders :
    /\ o \notin (Range(queue) \cup inEngine \cup matched)
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, o)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inEngine, matched, rejected>>

\* Backpressure signal: a submission attempted while the queue is saturated is
\* explicitly refused and recorded, instead of silently dropped or buffered.
Reject ==
  \E o \in Orders :
    /\ o \notin (Range(queue) \cup inEngine \cup matched)
    /\ Len(queue) >= Cap
    /\ rejected' = rejected \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inEngine, matched>>

\* The matching engine is the critical resource: only the queue head may take
\* it, and only while it is free.
BeginMatch ==
  /\ inEngine = {}
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ inEngine' = {Head(queue)}
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<matched, rejected>>

FinishMatch ==
  /\ inEngine # {}
  /\ matched' = matched \cup inEngine
  /\ inEngine' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, rejected>>

Next == Submit \/ Reject \/ BeginMatch \/ FinishMatch

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(BeginMatch) /\ WF_vars(FinishMatch)

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: the engine holds at most one
\* order, and that order is not simultaneously recorded anywhere else.
EngineMutex ==
  /\ \A o1 \in inEngine, o2 \in inEngine : o1 = o2
  /\ \A o \in inEngine : o \notin Range(queue) /\ o \notin matched

\* Liveness: every order admitted into the queue is eventually matched.
EventualMatch == \A o \in Orders : (o \in Range(queue)) ~> (o \in matched)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Orders = {o1, o2, o3}
  Cap = 2
INVARIANT EngineMutex
PROPERTY EventualMatch
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A stock exchange runs a single-instrument opening auction. Broker gateways submit order messages into a bounded work queue in front of the matching engine; the queue has finite capacity, so once it is full further submissions are explicitly refused (backpressure) rather than silently buffered. Order identifiers carry no intrinsic timestamp, and the network path from gateways to the queue can reorder messages in flight, so orders may be admitted into the queue in any relative order regardless of when brokers actually sent them. The matching engine itself is a single critical resource: only the order at the head of the queue may acquire it, and it must fully finish being matched (and release the engine) before the next order can be pulled in. Once an order finishes matching it is recorded as matched and never touched again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The matching engine holds at most one order at a time, and whichever order currently holds the engine is not simultaneously still sitting in the queue or already recorded as matched.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every order that is admitted into the queue is eventually recorded as matched by the engine.

---- MODULE W4Od16m8p3t0 ----
\* Pharmacy dispenser: hierarchical locking (coarse shelf lock, then fine slot
\* lock) guards slot allocation. A worker that crashes silently stops issuing
\* requests AND stops releasing whatever it still holds, so locks can freeze
\* forever. NoDoubleAllocation checks that this frozen-lock hazard never lets
\* two workers believe they both allocated the same slot.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Workers, NumShelves, SlotsPerShelf, NoWorker

ASSUME NoWorker \notin Workers

\* Shelves and slots are ranges sized by the two bounds; each shelf owns a
\* contiguous run of SlotsPerShelf slots, which is how ShelfOf groups them.
Shelves == 1..NumShelves
Slots == 1..(NumShelves * SlotsPerShelf)
ShelfOf(s) == ((s - 1) \div SlotsPerShelf) + 1

VARIABLES coarseHolder, fineHolder, allocatedBy, crashed

vars == <<coarseHolder, fineHolder, allocatedBy, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarseHolder \in [Shelves -> Workers \cup {NoWorker}]
  /\ fineHolder \in [Slots -> Workers \cup {NoWorker}]
  /\ allocatedBy \in [Slots -> SUBSET Workers]
  /\ crashed \subseteq Workers

Init ==
  /\ coarseHolder = [sh \in Shelves |-> NoWorker]
  /\ fineHolder = [s \in Slots |-> NoWorker]
  /\ allocatedBy = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
  /\ crashed = {}

\* Coarse step of the hierarchy: claim the whole shelf before any slot on it.
AcquireCoarse ==
  \E w \in Workers, sh \in Shelves :
    /\ w \notin crashed
    /\ coarseHolder[sh] = NoWorker
    /\ coarseHolder' = [coarseHolder EXCEPT ![sh] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineHolder, allocatedBy, crashed>>

\* Fine step: only the holder of the enclosing shelf's coarse lock may take it.
AcquireFine ==
  \E w \in Workers, s \in Slots :
    /\ w \notin crashed
    /\ coarseHolder[ShelfOf(s)] = w
    /\ fineHolder[s] = NoWorker
    /\ fineHolder' = [fineHolder EXCEPT ![s] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, allocatedBy, crashed>>

Allocate ==
  \E w \in Workers, s \in Slots :
    /\ w \notin crashed
    /\ fineHolder[s] = w
    /\ allocatedBy[s] = {}
    /\ allocatedBy' = [allocatedBy EXCEPT ![s] = {w}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, fineHolder, crashed>>

ReleaseFine ==
  \E w \in Workers, s \in Slots :
    /\ w \notin crashed
    /\ fineHolder[s] = w
    /\ fineHolder' = [fineHolder EXCEPT ![s] = NoWorker]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, allocatedBy, crashed>>

ReleaseCoarse ==
  \E w \in Workers, sh \in Shelves :
    /\ w \notin crashed
    /\ coarseHolder[sh] = w
    /\ \A s \in Slots : ShelfOf(s) = sh => fineHolder[s] # w
    /\ coarseHolder' = [coarseHolder EXCEPT ![sh] = NoWorker]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineHolder, allocatedBy, crashed>>

\* Twist: a worker crashes silently -- from then on it issues no more requests
\* and, unlike an orderly shutdown, never releases what it is still holding.
Crash ==
  \E w \in Workers :
    /\ w \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseHolder, fineHolder, allocatedBy>>

Next == AcquireCoarse \/ AcquireFine \/ Allocate \/ ReleaseFine \/ ReleaseCoarse \/ Crash

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: at most one worker is ever recorded as having
\* allocated any given slot.
NoDoubleAllocation == \A s \in Slots : \A w1, w2 \in allocatedBy[s] : w1 = w2

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Workers = {w1, w2}
  NumShelves = 2
  SlotsPerShelf = 2
  NoWorker = none
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A pharmacy's automated dispenser stores medication in numbered slots grouped onto shelves. A dispensing worker must acquire locks hierarchically: first a coarse-grained lock on the whole shelf that contains the target slot, then a fine-grained lock on that specific slot, before it is allowed to allocate the slot to a prescription. After allocating, the worker may release the fine lock and, once it holds no more fine locks on that shelf, the coarse shelf lock too. Any one dispensing worker may crash silently at any point: once crashed it issues no further requests and, critically, never releases any lock it is still holding, so that shelf or slot can become permanently unavailable to everyone else. Workers that have not crashed continue operating around whatever remains locked.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No slot is ever allocated to more than one dispensing worker at the same time, even though a crashed worker may be left holding coarse or fine locks forever.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m4p5t0 ----
\* Crane yard: a bounded work queue with backpressure feeds lift jobs to crane
\* operators. Lifting a container is irreversible, so AtMostOnceLift checks the
\* permanent lift log never records the same container twice, even though
\* exactly one operator may crash silently mid-lift and leave a job orphaned.
\* EventualLift is the progress guarantee: recovery must still get every
\* queued container lifted.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Jobs, Operators, Cap, NoJob

VARIABLES queue, assignedJob, liftLog, crashed, orphaned

vars == <<queue, assignedJob, liftLog, crashed, orphaned>>

Range(s) == {s[i] : i \in 1..Len(s)}

AssignedJobs == {assignedJob[op] : op \in Operators} \ {NoJob}

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(Jobs)
  /\ assignedJob \in [Operators -> Jobs \cup {NoJob}]
  /\ liftLog \in Seq(Jobs)
  /\ crashed \subseteq Operators
  /\ orphaned \subseteq Jobs

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ assignedJob = [op \in Operators |-> NoJob]
  /\ liftLog = <<>>
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ orphaned = {}

\* Backpressure: a container enters the bounded queue only while there is room.
Enqueue ==
  \E j \in Jobs :
    /\ j \notin (Range(queue) \cup AssignedJobs \cup Range(liftLog) \cup orphaned)
    /\ Len(queue) < Cap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, j)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assignedJob, liftLog, crashed, orphaned>>

\* A free, non-crashed operator claims the job at the head of the queue.
Assign ==
  \E op \in Operators :
    /\ op \notin crashed
    /\ assignedJob[op] = NoJob
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ assignedJob' = [assignedJob EXCEPT ![op] = Head(queue)]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<liftLog, crashed, orphaned>>

\* Irreversible action: the lift is recorded permanently and can never repeat.
Lift ==
  \E op \in Operators :
    /\ op \notin crashed
    /\ assignedJob[op] # NoJob
    /\ liftLog' = Append(liftLog, assignedJob[op])
    /\ assignedJob' = [assignedJob EXCEPT ![op] = NoJob]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed, orphaned>>

\* Twist: exactly one operator may crash silently while still holding a job.
Crash ==
  \E op \in Operators :
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = {op}
    /\ orphaned' = IF assignedJob[op] # NoJob
                   THEN orphaned \cup {assignedJob[op]}
                   ELSE orphaned
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, assignedJob, liftLog>>

\* A surviving operator recovers an orphaned job, guarding against re-lifting
\* one the crashed operator actually finished before it went silent.
Recover ==
  \E op \in Operators, j \in orphaned :
    /\ op \notin crashed
    /\ assignedJob[op] = NoJob
    /\ j \notin Range(liftLog)
    /\ assignedJob' = [assignedJob EXCEPT ![op] = j]
    /\ orphaned' = orphaned \ {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, liftLog, crashed>>

Next == Enqueue \/ Assign \/ Lift \/ Crash \/ Recover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Assign) /\ WF_vars(Lift) /\ WF_vars(Recover)

\* Safety: the permanent lift log never records the same container twice.
AtMostOnceLift == \A i, k \in 1..Len(liftLog) : i # k => liftLog[i] # liftLog[k]

\* Liveness: every container admitted to the queue is eventually lifted.
EventualLift == \A j \in Jobs : (j \in Range(queue)) ~> (j \in Range(liftLog))

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Jobs = {j1, j2, j3}
  Operators = {op1, op2}
  Cap = 2
  NoJob = none
INVARIANT AtMostOnceLift
PROPERTY EventualLift
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard feeds lift jobs (one per container) through a bounded work queue in front of the yard's gantry cranes. When a queue slot is free a free crane operator pulls the job at the front of the queue and takes ownership of it. Physically lifting a container off the ship is irreversible, so once an operator finishes a lift it is appended to a permanent lift log and that container must never be lifted again. Exactly one crane operator may crash silently while holding an assigned-but-not-yet-lifted job: the job is left orphaned, still unlifted, with no operator working it. A surviving, non-crashed operator can pick up an orphaned job -- but only if the lift log shows it was never actually completed -- and carry it through to a lift.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The permanent lift log never contains the same container twice, i.e. every container's irreversible lift happens at most once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every container admitted into the queue is eventually recorded in the lift log.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m3p1t4 ----
\* Interbank settlement batch: leader election with failover coordinates who
\* may apply pending instructions to the shared ledger record. A failover must
\* recycle whatever the old leader had mid-applied back into the pending pool
\* instead of discarding it. NoLostUpdates checks every submitted instruction
\* stays accounted for somewhere, even as the admission capacity is resized
\* at runtime.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Updates, MinCap, MaxCap, MaxTerm, NoUpdate

ASSUME NoUpdate \notin Updates
ASSUME MinCap \in Nat /\ MaxCap \in Nat /\ MinCap <= MaxCap
ASSUME MaxTerm \in Nat

VARIABLES term, pending, applied, inFlightUpdate, capacity, everSeen

vars == <<term, pending, applied, inFlightUpdate, capacity, everSeen>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in Nat
  /\ pending \subseteq Updates
  /\ applied \subseteq Updates
  /\ inFlightUpdate \in Updates \cup {NoUpdate}
  /\ capacity \in MinCap..MaxCap
  /\ everSeen \subseteq Updates

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ applied = {}
  /\ inFlightUpdate = NoUpdate
  /\ capacity = MinCap
  /\ everSeen = {}

\* Failover: a new term begins, and any instruction the old leader had pulled
\* out but not yet applied is put back into the pending pool, never dropped.
Elect ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ pending' = IF inFlightUpdate # NoUpdate THEN pending \cup {inFlightUpdate} ELSE pending
  /\ inFlightUpdate' = NoUpdate
  /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, capacity, everSeen>>

\* Admission is bounded by the current (resizable) capacity of the batch.
Submit ==
  \E u \in Updates :
    /\ u \notin everSeen
    /\ Cardinality(pending) < capacity
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {u}
    /\ everSeen' = everSeen \cup {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, applied, inFlightUpdate, capacity>>

\* Only while a leader exists (term > 0) may an instruction be pulled for work.
BeginApply ==
  /\ term > 0
  /\ inFlightUpdate = NoUpdate
  /\ pending # {}
  /\ \E u \in pending :
       /\ inFlightUpdate' = u
       /\ pending' = pending \ {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, applied, capacity, everSeen>>

FinishApply ==
  /\ term > 0
  /\ inFlightUpdate # NoUpdate
  /\ applied' = applied \cup {inFlightUpdate}
  /\ inFlightUpdate' = NoUpdate
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, pending, capacity, everSeen>>

\* Twist: the batch's admission capacity is resized at runtime, within bounds.
ChangeCapacity ==
  \E c \in MinCap..MaxCap :
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, pending, applied, inFlightUpdate, everSeen>>

Next == Elect \/ Submit \/ BeginApply \/ FinishApply \/ ChangeCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: every instruction ever submitted is currently accounted
\* for in the pending pool, the leader's in-progress slot, or the ledger.
NoLostUpdates == everSeen \subseteq (pending \cup {inFlightUpdate} \cup applied)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Updates = {u1, u2, u3}
  MinCap = 1
  MaxCap = 3
  MaxTerm = 3
  NoUpdate = none
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A consortium of banks runs an interbank settlement batch against a shared ledger record. A coordinating bank is elected leader, identified by an increasing term number, and only the current leader may pull a pending settlement instruction and apply it to the ledger. Instructions are first submitted into a pending pool bounded by the batch's admission capacity, and that capacity can be resized up or down while the batch is still running (an operations team widening or narrowing the settlement window mid-run). If the leader fails over -- a new election raises the term number and hands leadership to a (possibly different) bank -- whatever instruction the old leader had pulled out and was still mid-applying is not thrown away: it is put back into the pending pool so the new leader can pick it up and finish it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every settlement instruction that has ever been submitted is, at all times, accounted for in exactly the pending pool, the leader's in-progress slot, or the ledger's applied set -- never in none of them -- so no update is ever lost across an election or a capacity change.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m7p5t0 ----
\* Print-shop spooler: a single compare-and-swap register serializes which job
\* is claimed for printing. Printing is irreversible, so AtMostOncePrint checks
\* the permanent print log never records a job twice, even though exactly one
\* worker may crash silently mid-claim. EventualPrint is the progress promise:
\* a surviving worker must still be able to reset a stuck claim (after
\* checking the log) and get every backlog job printed.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Workers, NumJobs, NoJob

Jobs == 1..NumJobs

ASSUME NoJob \notin Jobs

VARIABLES registerOwner, workerJob, unclaimed, printLog, crashed

vars == <<registerOwner, workerJob, unclaimed, printLog, crashed>>

Range(s) == {s[i] : i \in 1..Len(s)}

\* The oldest (lowest-id) unclaimed job is always the next one offered up.
NextJob == CHOOSE j \in unclaimed : \A j2 \in unclaimed : j <= j2

TypeOK ==
  /\ registerOwner \in Jobs \cup {NoJob}
  /\ workerJob \in [Workers -> Jobs \cup {NoJob}]
  /\ unclaimed \subseteq Jobs
  /\ printLog \in Seq(Jobs)
  /\ crashed \subseteq Workers

Init ==
  /\ registerOwner = NoJob
  /\ workerJob = [w \in Workers |-> NoJob]
  /\ unclaimed = {}
  /\ printLog = <<>>
  /\ crashed = {}

\* A submitted job joins the backlog once, if it has never been seen before.
Submit ==
  \E j \in Jobs :
    /\ j \notin unclaimed
    /\ j \notin Range(printLog)
    /\ j # registerOwner
    /\ \A w \in Workers : workerJob[w] # j
    /\ unclaimed' = unclaimed \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<registerOwner, workerJob, printLog, crashed>>

\* Compare-and-swap: the claim only succeeds if the register was still empty.
ClaimCAS ==
  \E w \in Workers :
    /\ w \notin crashed
    /\ workerJob[w] = NoJob
    /\ registerOwner = NoJob
    /\ unclaimed # {}
    /\ registerOwner' = NextJob
    /\ workerJob' = [workerJob EXCEPT ![w] = NextJob]
    /\ unclaimed' = unclaimed \ {NextJob}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printLog, crashed>>

\* Irreversible action: the print is recorded permanently and never repeats.
Print ==
  \E w \in Workers :
    /\ w \notin crashed
    /\ workerJob[w] # NoJob
    /\ printLog' = Append(printLog, workerJob[w])
    /\ registerOwner' = NoJob
    /\ workerJob' = [workerJob EXCEPT ![w] = NoJob]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unclaimed, crashed>>

\* Twist: exactly one worker may crash silently while still holding a claim.
Crash ==
  \E w \in Workers :
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashed' = {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<registerOwner, workerJob, unclaimed, printLog>>

\* A surviving worker resets the stuck register, but only once the print log
\* proves the crashed worker's job was never actually finished.
ResetClaim ==
  \E wc \in crashed :
    /\ workerJob[wc] # NoJob
    /\ workerJob[wc] \notin Range(printLog)
    /\ registerOwner' = NoJob
    /\ workerJob' = [workerJob EXCEPT ![wc] = NoJob]
    /\ unclaimed' = unclaimed \cup {workerJob[wc]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printLog, crashed>>

Next == Submit \/ ClaimCAS \/ Print \/ Crash \/ ResetClaim

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(ClaimCAS) /\ WF_vars(Print) /\ WF_vars(ResetClaim)

\* Safety: the permanent print log never records the same job twice.
AtMostOncePrint == \A i, k \in 1..Len(printLog) : i # k => printLog[i] # printLog[k]

\* Liveness: every backlog job is eventually printed.
EventualPrint == \A j \in Jobs : (j \in unclaimed) ~> (j \in Range(printLog))

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Workers = {w1, w2}
  NumJobs = 3
  NoJob = none
INVARIANT AtMostOncePrint
PROPERTY EventualPrint
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A print shop spooler holds jobs waiting to be printed. Instead of a lock, the shop uses a single shared compare-and-swap register that names at most one job as currently "claimed": a print worker may only take a job by successfully swapping the register from empty to that job's id, which succeeds only if the register was actually still empty at that instant. Printing a claimed job onto paper is irreversible, so once a worker finishes printing, the job id is appended to a permanent print log and that job must never be printed again. Exactly one print worker may crash silently while it still holds a claim: the register stays pointed at that job forever unless a surviving worker resets it, and a reset is only allowed after checking the print log to confirm the job was never actually finished, so a crash can never cause a reprint. Jobs are always claimed in increasing id order, so the oldest unclaimed job is always the next one offered to the register.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the permanent print log never contains the same job id twice, i.e. every job's irreversible print happens at most once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every job that enters the spooler's unclaimed backlog is eventually recorded in the print log.
