  AdminTok = admintok
  MaxAdminOverrides = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A clearing consortium of correspondent banks runs a nightly interbank
settlement batch. Each settlement slot in the batch represents a net-position
transfer that must be assigned to exactly one bank for execution. Before a
slot can be assigned, participating banks cast quorum votes for it; once at
least Quorum distinct banks have voted for a slot, any one of those voting
banks may be granted the lease on that slot. A bank holding a slot may
release it back to the pool at any time, freeing it for a future round of
voting. The batch operator can also close the voting window for the batch
(after which ordinary voting and allocation stop), and a privileged admin
account can override the normal process at any time: the admin may seize an
unleased slot directly without waiting for a quorum, and the admin may force
the batch back open even after it has been closed. Crucially, the admin's
override path is still required to check that a slot is not already held by
someone else before seizing it -- the override bypasses the voting and
batch-closed rules, but it never bypasses the check that prevents a slot
from having two simultaneous holders.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every point in time, each settlement slot has at most
one active holder (an ordinary bank or the admin), regardless of whether
that holder was assigned through normal quorum voting or through the
privileged admin override.

  /\ snapshot \in [Routers -> [Bags -> Nat]]

CONSTANTS
  Routers = {r1, r2}
  Bags = {bag1, bag2}
  MaxRetries = 2
  NoRouter = norouter

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AtMostOnce
PROPERTY EventuallyRouted
nl:
An airport baggage router assigns each bag on the belt to exactly one outgoing
chute; once a bag has been physically diverted onto a chute this routing
decision is irreversible, so it must never be executed twice for the same
bag. Each bag has a small compare-and-swap register that starts at version 0.
A router node optimistically inspects a bag's register, caching a local
snapshot of its version. If the router later finds its cached snapshot is
stale (because some other router has already committed the routing decision
for that bag), it refreshes its snapshot and retries, instead of blocking.
A router commits the routing decision for a bag only if its cached snapshot
still matches the live register at the moment it acts; that commit bumps the
register's version and permanently records which router routed the bag.
Because no locks are ever held, the protocol tolerates one router node
crashing silently at any point without warning the others: a crashed router
simply stops taking any further steps, but it never holds up another
router's optimistic attempt on any bag. Once every bag on the belt has been
routed, the system settles into a quiescent state.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every bag, its compare-and-swap register is committed
at most once, and the register reads as committed exactly when the bag has
an assigned router.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag on the belt is eventually routed to some chute,
even though one router node may crash silently at any point during the
protocol.

  /\ queue \in Seq(Machines)
  /\ Len(queue) <= Capacity
  /\ dropped \in 0..MaxDropped
  /\ inService \in Machines \cup {NoMachine}

Init ==
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ dropped = 0
  /\ inService = NoMachine

Send(m) ==
  /\ m \notin inflight
  /\ m \notin Range(queue)
  /\ inService # m
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, dropped, inService>>

Deliver(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, m)
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<dropped, inService>>

DropOnFull(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ Len(queue) >= Capacity
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ dropped' = IF dropped < MaxDropped THEN dropped + 1 ELSE dropped
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inService>>

Serve ==
  /\ inService = NoMachine
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ inService' = Head(queue)
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, dropped>>

FinishService ==
  /\ inService # NoMachine
  /\ inService' = NoMachine
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, queue, dropped>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Send(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Deliver(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : DropOnFull(m)
  \/ Serve
  \/ FinishService

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

QueueBounded == Len(queue) <= Capacity

CONSTANTS
  Machines = {m1, m2, m3}
  Capacity = 2
  MaxDropped = 2
  NoMachine = nomachine

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT QueueBounded
nl:
A network of vending machines reports low-stock events to a central
replenishment worker over an unreliable, unordered network. Each machine may
have at most one restock request outstanding at a time: once it emits a
request onto the network, it will not emit another until that request has
either landed in the worker's bounded work queue, been dropped, or been
pulled into service. Because the network does not preserve send order,
any currently in-flight request may be the next one to land in the queue,
so requests can arrive at the worker in a different order than they were
sent. The worker's work queue has a fixed, bounded capacity: an in-flight
request can only be admitted into the queue while there is room in it. When
the queue is already full, the network instead exercises backpressure by
dropping the in-flight request rather than letting it overflow the queue.
The worker processes requests one at a time, pulling the oldest queued
request into service and later completing that service, which frees the
worker to pull the next one.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of restock requests held in the worker's bounded
work queue never exceeds its declared capacity, regardless of how the
reordering network schedules deliveries.

  /\ phase \in {"prepare", "committed", "aborted"}
  /\ votes \subseteq Cars

  /\ crashed \subseteq Cars

  /\ c \notin votes

CONSTANTS
  Cars = {c1, c2}
  MaxEpoch = 3
  NoCar = nocar

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleExecution
PROPERTY EventuallyResolves
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper assigns floor-call rounds to its cars using
a two-phase commit protocol coordinated by the bank controller. At the start
of a round the controller stamps a fresh round epoch; each car must first
sync its local view to that epoch before it is allowed to cast its
prepare-vote for the round. Once every surviving car has voted, the
controller commits the round; only after commit may a car that voted for it
actually execute the floor call (open its doors and serve the call) --
and it may only do so while its own locally synced epoch still matches the
controller's current epoch. A car whose local epoch has fallen behind
(for instance because a new round already started before it got around to
acting) is stale, and it must never be allowed to execute a floor call under
an epoch that is no longer current. The bank controller does not wait
forever on a car that has gone silent: if a car has crashed, the controller
times out the prepare phase and aborts the round rather than blocking on a
vote that will never arrive, and then proceeds to open the next round.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No car ever executes a floor call while its locally synced
epoch differs from the controller's current epoch -- only a currently
authorized, non-stale participant may act.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The controller never blocks in the prepare phase forever;
every round it starts eventually resolves to committed or aborted, even
though exactly one elevator car may crash silently at any point.

CONSTANTS Locations, Cranes, Total, StartLoc, MaxVersion, MaxRetries

RECURSIVE SumSet(_, _)
SumSet(S, f) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE
       IN f[x] + SumSet(S \ {x}, f)

VARIABLES count, version, grasped, dest, cache, retries

vars == <<count, version, grasped, dest, cache, retries>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ count \in [Locations -> 0..Total]
  /\ version \in [Locations -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ grasped \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ dest \in [Cranes -> Locations]
  /\ cache \in [Cranes -> [Locations -> 0..MaxVersion]]
  /\ retries \in [Cranes -> 0..MaxRetries]

Init ==
  /\ count = [l \in Locations |-> IF l = StartLoc THEN Total ELSE 0]
  /\ version = [l \in Locations |-> 0]
  /\ grasped = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
  /\ dest = [c \in Cranes |-> StartLoc]
  /\ cache = [c \in Cranes |-> [l \in Locations |-> 0]]
  /\ retries = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]

Bump(v) == IF v < MaxVersion THEN v + 1 ELSE v

Inspect(c, l) ==
  /\ ~grasped[c]
  /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![c][l] = version[l]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<count, version, grasped, dest, retries>>

Retry(c, l) ==
  /\ ~grasped[c]
  /\ cache[c][l] # version[l]
  /\ cache' = [cache EXCEPT ![c][l] = version[l]]
  /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![c] = IF @ < MaxRetries THEN @ + 1 ELSE @]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<count, version, grasped, dest>>

Lift(c, l, d) ==
  /\ ~grasped[c]
  /\ cache[c][l] = version[l]
  /\ count[l] > 0
  /\ count' = [count EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![l] = Bump(@)]
  /\ grasped' = [grasped EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ dest' = [dest EXCEPT ![c] = d]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cache, retries>>

SetDown(c) ==
  /\ grasped[c]
  /\ count' = [count EXCEPT ![dest[c]] = @ + 1]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![dest[c]] = Bump(@)]
  /\ grasped' = [grasped EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cache, dest, retries>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, l \in Locations : Inspect(c, l)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, l \in Locations : Retry(c, l)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes, l \in Locations, d \in Locations : Lift(c, l, d)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : SetDown(c)

CONSTANTS
  Locations = {ship, yardA}
  Cranes = {crane1, crane2}
  Total = 2
  StartLoc = ship
  MaxVersion = 1
  MaxRetries = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
A container-ship crane yard uses several gantry cranes to move containers
between the ship's hold and the yard stacks. Each stack keeps a
compare-and-swap version register that changes whenever the stack's
container count changes. Before lifting a container off a stack, a crane
optimistically watches that stack's register, caching the version it last
saw. Because instructions and status updates travel over a network that can
reorder them, a crane's cached watch of a stack can go stale by the time it
is ready to act -- another crane may have already lifted from (or set a
container down onto) that same stack in the meantime. When a crane notices
its cached version no longer matches the stack's live version, it re-syncs
its watch and retries instead of acting on stale information. A crane is
only granted a lift from a stack while its cached watch still agrees with
that stack's live register and the stack is non-empty; the lift removes one
container from the stack and leaves it held in the crane's grip, in transit
to a chosen destination stack. Setting the container down at the destination
adds it back onto a stack, completing the move. Containers are never
manufactured or scrapped in the yard: every one that leaves a stack is
either sitting in some crane's grip or has already landed on another stack.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every point in time, the total number of containers
resting on yard/ship/truck stacks plus the number currently held in a
crane's grip equals the fixed total number of containers in the yard
system -- no container is ever created or destroyed by a lift, a stale
retry, or a set-down, regardless of how the network reorders crane
messages.
